textbookText: 110. Which of the following is an assumption used in deriving/applying the ideal gas laws that real gases violate at high pressure? A) Gas molecules have negligible volume compared to the container B) Gas molecules have significant volume that must always be considered C) Gas molecules attract each other strongly at all pressures D) Gas laws assume molecules are always in a liquid state
111. Vapor density of a gas relates to its molar mass by: A) Molar mass = 2 × Vapor density B) Molar mass = Vapor density / 2 C) Molar mass = Vapor density² D) Molar mass = Vapor density × R
112. A gas occupies 2 L at 1 atm. If pressure is increased to 4 atm at constant temperature, the new volume is (Boyle's law): A) 0.5 L B) 8 L C) 2 L D) 4 L
113. If a gas at 300 K and volume 1 L is heated to 600 K at constant pressure, its new volume (Charles's law) is: A) 2 L B) 0.5 L C) 1 L D) 4 L

114. Which gas law would you invoke to explain why the pressure inside a sealed rigid container increases when heated? A) Gay-Lussac's law (pressure-temperature law at constant volume) B) Boyle's law C) Charles's law D) Graham's law

115. Molar volume from the ideal gas law at STP (22.4 L) can be derived by substituting into PV = nRT with: A) n = 1 mol, T = 273.15 K, P = 1 atm, solving for V B) n = 6.022×10²³ mol C) T = 0 K D) P = 0 atm

116. Which of these statements about an "ideal gas" is correct? A) It is a hypothetical gas that perfectly obeys the gas laws at all temperatures and pressures, with no intermolecular forces and point-sized particles B) It is any real gas at room temperature C) It only exists at absolute zero D) It has significant intermolecular attraction by definition

117. Why do helium balloons deflate faster than air-filled balloons of the same material (extraordinary application of Graham's law)? A) Helium's low molar mass gives it a higher rate of diffusion/effusion through tiny pores in the balloon B) Helium reacts chemically with the balloon material C) Helium has a higher molar mass than air D) Helium condenses into liquid inside the balloon

118. The equation of state for n moles of an ideal gas, PV = nRT, was essentially unified from Boyle's, Charles's, and Avogadro's laws by: A) Combining them into a single comprehensive relation involving all four variables P, V, n, T B) Discarding Avogadro's law entirely C) Using only Dalton's law D) Applying Graham's law of diffusion
119. If the total pressure of a gas mixture of N₂ and O₂ is 1 atm, and the mole fraction of O₂ is 0.2, the partial pressure of O₂ is: A) 0.2 atm B) 1 atm C) 0.8 atm D) 5 atm

120. A key limitation shared by Boyle's, Charles's, and Gay-Lussac's laws is that they: A) Are only strictly valid for ideal gases and deviate for real gases, especially at high pressure/low temperature B) Apply exactly to all real gases under any condition C) Do not apply to any real gas ever, even approximately D) Only work for liquids, not gases
